newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FIRM SELLS SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM TO S.AFRICAN SCHOOLS.
newsitem.headline: FIRM SELLS SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM TO S.AFRICAN SCHOOLS.

text.p: A private company sought to convince schools in violence-plagued South Africa on Tuesday to put television cameras in every corner to protect their pupils from danger.

British-based Telecom Sciences Corporation (TSc) said at the launch of a new hi-tech security system that its "SafetyNet" could also bring the Internet and ISDN high-quality telephone lines to every classroom.
TSc said it could link up every classroom, corridor and playground at an affordable cost to cut burglary and vandalism and help teachers dealing with intruders, unruly pupils or in any emergency.
"The security situation in South Africa has reached such proportions that...a product like SafetyNet will contribute greatly to a secure environment," it said in a statement.
"Tragedies such as the Dunblane massacre in Scotland have served to illustrate the need for something to be done to protect our youngsters."
A gunman shot dead a classroom of young children in the massacre last year, one of Britain's worst.
Eric Henderson of Netcom Solutions, a local partner to TSc, said they were involved in negotiations with about 12 schools in Gauteng province for a pilot study over the next six weeks.
A national education spokesman was not able to comment on the security system before investigating the product's usefulness, but in general encouraged the use of technology in schools.
